record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: In knowledge-base mapping generation, how can mapping rules be generated for metadata-data correspondences, where a source data value must become target metadata such as a property name, or target data must become metadata, rather than simply mapping source concepts, properties, or paths to target concepts, properties, or paths?

evidence.quote: One important type of correspondence that, to the best of our knowledge, is not considered in KMGTs is metadata-data (MAD) correspondences [40,51]. Such correspondences articulate the need for a mapping that transforms data values to metadata (e.g., a property name) or vice versa. Arguably, such transformations may be more prevalent in KBs than in relational or semi-structured models. Generating proper mappings from MAD correspondences can be challenging.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of automatically generating mapping rules between two knowledge bases (KBs), each modeled as a set of concepts, properties, and instance data, together with a schema (metadata) layer naming the concepts and properties. A standard schema-level correspondence between a source KB S and a target KB T relates a source schema element (concept, property, or path) to a target schema element, and induces data-to-data mapping rules.

A metadata-data (MAD) correspondence, by contrast, asserts one of the following relationships:
(i) a source data value v occurring as an instance value in S must appear as a target metadata symbol in T (for example, as the name of a property or a class in T), or
(ii) a target data value must be produced from a source metadata symbol (for example, the name of a property in S must appear as data in T).

Develop a formal framework and algorithm for knowledge-base mapping generation that, given a set of correspondences between S and T including MAD correspondences, produces executable mapping rules whose execution on instances of S yields instances of T consistent with all correspondences. In particular:

1. Provide a precise semantics for MAD correspondences within a chosen KB data model (e.g., RDF/RDFS or OWL).
2. Define when a set of generated mapping rules is sound and complete with respect to a set of correspondences that may mix schema-level and MAD correspondences.
3. Give a generation procedure that handles MAD correspondences in both directions (data→metadata and metadata→data) and analyze its correctness and complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns generating mapping rules for metadata-data (MAD) correspondences in knowledge-base mapping generation tools (KMGTs). This is identified as an open problem not addressed by existing KMGTs, and no subsequent work resolving it in full generality was located.
